title: SaaS / tech
objectives: Answer out loud: What's the Rule of 40?

steps.body: High-growth software companies often have low or negative current profits, so EV/revenue (often NTM) is common.
Key metrics: ARR, net revenue retention, gross retention, CAC payback, LTV/CAC, Rule of 40.
Subscription revenue creates deferred revenue (negative working capital).

blocks.template: Rule of 40: revenue growth % + profit margin % should be {{1}}
NRR above {{1}} means existing customers grow revenue even after churn

blocks.title: What's net revenue retention?
blocks.teaser: Revenue this year from customers who existed a year ago ÷ their revenue last year.
blocks.body:
Revenue this year from customers who existed a year ago ÷ their revenue last year. Includes upsells and churn. 120% means the existing base grew 20% on its own. It's one of the strongest drivers of SaaS multiples.

**Interview answer:** "Revenue from last year's customers this year over last year — above 100% means the existing base grows even after churn."

blocks.prompt: A SaaS company's net revenue retention is 120%. What does that mean?

options.text: It added 20% more customers this year
Last year's customers generate 20% more revenue this year, even after churn
It lost 20% of customers but raised prices

blocks.explanation: NRR = this year's revenue from last year's customers ÷ their revenue last year. 120% means the existing base grew 20% on its own.

blocks.title: What's the Rule of 40?
blocks.teaser: Growth rate + profit margin (usually EBITDA or FCF margin) ≥ 40%.
blocks.body: Growth rate + profit margin (usually EBITDA or FCF margin) ≥ 40%. It captures the tradeoff: a company growing 50% can lose 10%; one growing 10% should earn 30%.

blocks.title: LTV/CAC?
blocks.teaser: Lifetime value of a customer ÷ cost to acquire them.
blocks.body: Lifetime value of a customer ÷ cost to acquire them. Above ~3x is generally considered healthy. CAC payback (months to recover acquisition cost) is the related metric.

blocks.title: Why is SBC a bigger issue for tech valuations?
blocks.teaser: Tech companies pay a large share of compensation in stock.
blocks.body: Tech companies pay a large share of compensation in stock. Adjusted EBITDA that adds back SBC can make an unprofitable company look profitable. Investors increasingly subtract it.
